purpose: Norethindrone is used as a birth control pill to prevent pregnancy, and it can also be used to treat irregular or painful periods and a condition called endometriosis. It is sometimes called the 'mini-pill' because it contains only one hormone instead of two.
how_it_works: Norethindrone works by mimicking a natural hormone in your body called progesterone. It thickens the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time reaching an egg, and it can also prevent your ovaries from releasing an egg. Together, these effects make it very difficult for pregnancy to occur.
common_side_effects: Irregular bleeding or spotting between periods (this is very common, especially at first), headaches, nausea, breast tenderness, mood changes, acne, and changes in sex drive. Your periods may become lighter or stop altogether, which is normal with this medication.
warnings: Take your pill at the SAME TIME every day — even being 3 hours late can reduce its effectiveness. Tell your doctor if you have a history of breast cancer, liver disease, or unexplained vaginal bleeding. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). If you miss a pill, use a backup method like condoms for 48 hours. Contact your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain, as there is a small risk of ectopic pregnancy.
typical_dosing: For birth control, the usual dose is one 0.35 mg tablet taken by mouth every day at exactly the same time each day, with no breaks between pill packs. For other conditions like endometriosis, the dose may be higher (2.5 to 10 mg daily) and your doctor will give you specific instructions.
